exam_set.title: Practice Set 1
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 10, Practice Set 1

questions.jp: 1.5Mビット／秒の伝送路を用いて12Mバイトのデータを転送するのに必要な伝送時間は何秒か。ここで、伝送路の伝送効率を50%とする。
questions.romaji: 1.5 M bitto/byō no densōro o mochiite 12 M baito no dēta o tensō suru no ni hitsuyō na densō jikan wa nan-byō ka. Koko de, densōro no densō kōritsu o 50% to suru.
questions.en: How many seconds are needed to transfer 12 MB over a 1.5 Mbit/s link whose transmission efficiency is 50%?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Bytes become bits, then usable speed is halved. Divide data by usable speed.

Technical breakdown:
Rule: time = data bits / effective rate. 12 MB × 8 = 96 Mbit. Effective rate = 1.5 Mbit/s × 0.50 = 0.75 Mbit/s. 96 / 0.75 = 128 s.

Japanese keywords to remember:
伝送時間 = densō jikan = transmission time
伝送効率 = densō kōritsu = transmission efficiency

Why the best solution works:
エ gives 128 seconds after both byte-to-bit conversion and efficiency adjustment.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
16 ignores the 8-bit conversion and efficiency.
イ:
32 does not apply both required factors correctly.
ウ:
64 applies the byte-to-bit conversion but effectively ignores the 50% efficiency.

Memory trick:
Byte × 8; speed × efficiency; then divide.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: 1Gバイトの動画データを40Mビット／秒の回線を使用してダウンロードしたところ、5分掛かった。このときの回線利用率はおよそ何%か。ここで、ダウンロード時には動画データに20%の制御情報が付加されるものとする。
questions.romaji: 1 G baito no dōga dēta o 40 M bitto/byō no kaisen o shiyō shite daunrōdo shita tokoro, 5-fun kakatta. Kono toki no kaisen riyōritsu wa oyoso nan-pāsento ka. Koko de, daunrōdo-ji ni wa dōga dēta ni 20% no seigyo jōhō ga fuka sareru mono to suru.
questions.en: A 1 GB video takes 5 minutes to download over a 40 Mbit/s line. With 20% control overhead, approximately what is the line utilization?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Add overhead, convert bytes to bits, then compare actual traffic rate with line capacity.

Technical breakdown:
Transferred bits = 1 GB × 1.20 × 8 = 9.6 Gbit. Time = 5 min = 300 s. Actual rate = 9.6 Gbit / 300 s = 32 Mbit/s. Utilization = 32 / 40 × 100 = 80%.

Japanese keywords to remember:
回線利用率 = kaisen riyōritsu = line utilization
制御情報 = seigyo jōhō = control overhead

Why the best solution works:
エ is the calculated 80% utilization.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
10% confuses a ratio or conversion factor with utilization.
イ:
53% results from incomplete handling of units or overhead.
ウ:
67% omits the 20% control information.

Memory trick:
Traffic includes overhead; utilization = traffic rate / line rate.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: 本社と工場との間を専用線で接続してデータを伝送するシステムがある。このシステムでは2,000バイト／件の伝票データを2件ずつまとめ、それに400バイトのヘッダー情報を付加して送っている。伝票データは、1時間に平均100,000件発生している。回線速度を1Mビット／秒としたとき、回線利用率はおよそ何%か。
questions.romaji: Honsha to kōjō to no aida o sen'yōsen de setsuzoku shite dēta o densō suru shisutemu ga aru. Kono shisutemu de wa 2,000 baito/ken no denpyō dēta o 2-ken zutsu matome, sore ni 400 baito no heddā jōhō o fuka shite okutte iru. Denpyō dēta wa, 1-jikan ni heikin 100,000-ken hassei shite iru. Kaisen sokudo o 1 M bitto/byō to shita toki, kaisen riyōritsu wa oyoso nan-pāsento ka.
questions.en: A system batches two 2,000-byte records and adds a 400-byte header. With 100,000 records/hour and a 1 Mbit/s line, approximately what is utilization?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Every pair carries 4,000 bytes of data plus 400 bytes of header. Count all pairs per hour.

Technical breakdown:
100,000 records form 50,000 batches. One batch = 2,000 × 2 + 400 = 4,400 bytes. Hourly bits = 50,000 × 4,400 × 8 = 1.76 Gbit. Capacity/hour = 1 Mbit/s × 3,600 s = 3.6 Gbit. Utilization = 1.76/3.6 ×100 ≈ 48.9% ≈ 49%.

Japanese keywords to remember:
回線利用率 = kaisen riyōritsu = line utilization
ヘッダー情報 = heddā jōhō = header information

Why the best solution works:
ウ correctly includes one header per two records and gives about 49%.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
6.1% arises from losing the byte-to-bit factor.
イ:
44% ignores header traffic.
エ:
53% applies the header at an incorrect frequency or amount.

Memory trick:
Batch first, add header per batch, then convert to bits.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: メモリモジュールのパリティチェックの目的として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Memori mojūru no pariti chekku no mokuteki to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: What is the purpose of parity checking in a memory module?

options.label: ア
options.jp: メモリモジュールに電源が供給されているかどうかを判定する。
options.romaji: Memori mojūru ni dengen ga kyōkyū sarete iru ka dō ka o hantei suru.
options.en: Determine whether power is supplied to the memory module.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 読出し時に、エラーが発生したかどうかを検出する。
options.romaji: Yomidashi-ji ni, erā ga hassei shita ka dō ka o kenshutsu suru.
options.en: Detect whether an error occurred during reading.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 読出し時に、エラーを検出して自動的に訂正する。
options.romaji: Yomidashi-ji ni, erā o kenshutsu shite jidōteki ni teisei suru.
options.en: Detect and automatically correct an error during reading.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 読み出したデータを暗号化する。

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Parity is an alarm: it notices a changed bit, but does not repair it.

Technical breakdown:
A parity bit makes the number of 1s even or odd. On read, recomputing parity reveals a mismatch and therefore detects an error. Basic parity has no information locating the bad bit, so it cannot correct it.

Japanese keywords to remember:
パリティチェック = pariti chekku = parity check
誤り検出 = ayamari kenshutsu = error detection

Why the best solution works:
イ states the actual goal: detecting a read error.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Power presence is not determined by parity.
ウ:
Automatic correction requires an error-correcting code such as ECC, not basic parity.
エ:
Parity is error control, not encryption.

Memory trick:
Parity detects; ECC corrects.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 送信側では、ビット列をある生成多項式で割った余りをそのビット列に付加して送信し、受信側では、受信したビット列が同じ生成多項式で割り切れるか否かで誤りの発生を判断する誤り検査方式はどれか。
questions.romaji: Sōshin-gawa de wa, bittoretsu o aru seisei takōshiki de watta amari o sono bittoretsu ni fuka shite sōshin shi, jushin-gawa de wa, jushin shita bittoretsu ga onaji seisei takōshiki de warikireru ka ina ka de ayamari no hassei o handan suru ayamari kensa hōshiki wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which error-checking method appends the remainder from division by a generator polynomial and checks divisibility by the same polynomial at the receiver?

options.label: イ
options.jp: 垂直パリティチェック方式

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 水平パリティチェック方式

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Sender and receiver use the same polynomial division rule; a nonzero remainder signals damage.

Technical breakdown:
CRC treats the bit string as a polynomial over GF(2). The sender appends the generator-polynomial remainder. The receiver divides the received codeword by the same generator; a nonzero remainder indicates an error.

Japanese keywords to remember:
生成多項式 = seisei takōshiki = generator polynomial
余り = amari = remainder

Why the best solution works:
ア exactly describes cyclic redundancy check.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Vertical parity counts bit parity by a chosen unit; it does not use polynomial division.
ウ:
Horizontal parity also uses parity counts, not a generator polynomial.
エ:
Hamming code uses parity positions to locate and correct bit errors.

Memory trick:
Polynomial remainder means CRC.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: 通信回線の伝送誤りに対処するパリティチェック方式（垂直パリティ）の記述として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Tsūshin kaisen no densō ayamari ni taisho suru pariti chekku hōshiki (suichoku pariti) no kijutsu to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement correctly describes vertical parity checking for transmission errors on a communication line?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 1ビットの誤りを検出できる。
options.en: It can detect a one-bit error.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 1ビットの誤りを訂正でき、2ビットの誤りを検出できる。
options.romaji: 1-bitto no ayamari o teisei deki, 2-bitto no ayamari o kenshutsu dekiru.
options.en: It can correct a one-bit error and detect a two-bit error.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 奇数パリティならば1ビットの誤りを検出できるが、偶数パリティでは1ビットの誤りも検出できない。
options.romaji: Kisū pariti naraba 1-bitto no ayamari o kenshutsu dekiru ga, gūsū pariti de wa 1-bitto no ayamari mo kenshutsu dekinai.
options.en: Odd parity detects a one-bit error, but even parity cannot detect even a one-bit error.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 奇数パリティならば奇数個のビット誤りを、偶数パリティならば偶数個のビット誤りを検出できる。
options.romaji: Kisū pariti naraba kisūko no bitto ayamari o, gūsū pariti naraba gūsūko no bitto ayamari o kenshutsu dekiru.
options.en: Odd parity detects an odd number of bit errors, while even parity detects an even number.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Parity notices when flipping bits changes whether the count of 1s is odd or even. One flipped bit always changes it.

Technical breakdown:
Vertical parity fixes each checked unit to odd or even parity. Any odd number of bit flips reverses the parity, so it is detectable; a single-bit error is therefore always detected. An even number of flips can preserve the original parity and may go undetected. Basic parity detects but does not locate or correct errors.

Japanese keywords to remember:
垂直パリティ = suichoku pariti = vertical parity
伝送誤り = densō ayamari = transmission error

Why the best solution works:
ア is guaranteed true: one bit flip always reverses parity, for both odd and even parity schemes.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Basic parity cannot locate the erroneous bit, so it cannot correct one-bit errors; two-bit errors may be missed.
ウ:
Even parity also detects every single-bit error. Odd/even names define the expected count, not detection ability.
エ:
Both odd and even parity detect odd numbers of flips and may miss even numbers; detection does not depend on choosing matching odd/even counts.

Memory trick:
Odd number of flips changes parity; even number may hide.

Correct answer: ア
